layers.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India (e-FRRO portal)
layers.process: The area between the Inner Line and the international border is a Protected Area (Third Schedule). The Order traces the line along high ridges and rivers, including the Bhagirathi, Alaknanda, Dhauli Ganga and Gori Ganga, from Singa Ghati to the Kali and Gori Ganga junction on the Nepal border. Foreigners need a Protected Area Permit beyond it. Apply online at indianfrro.gov.in (the e-FRRO portal) or in the Indian Visa Su-Swagatam app; the permit is issued electronically. Citizens of Afghanistan, China or Pakistan, and people of origin there (born there, a parent or grandparent born and permanently living there, or ever a citizen), need the central government's prior approval. Smartraveller advises applying at least 4 weeks ahead; entering without a permit carries significant penalties.

layers.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India (e-FRRO portal)
layers.process: Listed Tibetan settlements, monasteries and institutions in and around Dehradun are Restricted Areas (Fourth Schedule): among them Clement Town (including Mindrolling and Tashi Kyil monasteries), Sahastradhara, Manduwala, Herbertpur and Lakhanwala, Nalapani, and the Sakya Centre and Tibetan Women Centre on Rajpur Road. Daytime visits are allowed without a permit if the settlement, monastery or institute gives the visitor's name, parentage, date of birth, nationality, passport and visa numbers to the Foreigners Registration Officer. Staying needs a Restricted Area Permit; foreign students can get one valid for 3 years if the institute vouches for them.
